v.rationale: All three share the same migration, the same Fillable change, the same correct FormRequest rules ('present','nullable','string','max:30') and the same update-from-validated() flow. All their test suites pass, and so do my six probes on each: whitespace-only, multibyte 31/30, real Sanctum token, integer input, form-encoded PATCH and PUT returning 405. What separates them is the response contract and the tests. impl-1 ranks first: its Resource with $wrap=null returns exactly {id,name,nickname}, and its tests are the most complete, including the real-token path and multibyte boundaries. impl-3 ranks second. It is the leanest and most proportionate design (only() plus tap()) with a correct flat contract, but it repeats the field list, keeps the stub docblocks, and has weaker tests: the boundary test doesn't check persistence and the guest checks are bundled into one test. impl-2 ranks third. Its tests are good and idiomatic with datasets, but its JsonResource keeps the default 'data' wrapper, so the endpoint doesn't return id/name/nickname at the top level as the spec states. The prefix('me')->get('/') routing also adds ceremony.
